sections.overview: The Sand Martin is a small migratory swallow breeding across much of the Northern Hemisphere.
sections.identification: It is brown above, pale below, with a distinct brown breast band.
sections.habitat: It nests in sandy riverbanks, coastal bluffs and suitable gravel pits or quarries.
sections.diet: It catches small flying insects, often while foraging low over water.
sections.behavior: It is social and migrates to Africa south of the Sahara for winter.
sections.reproduction: Pairs excavate a nesting tunnel in a soft bank and line the chamber at its end.
sections.ecology: Colonies depend on exposed, eroding banks; artificial sand and gravel workings can also provide nest sites.
sections.conservation: The 2025 global assessment lists it as Least Concern, although its population trend is decreasing.
